newsitem.title: UK: Thorn likely casualty in FTSE 100 shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Thorn likely casualty in FTSE 100 shake-up.

text.p: Less than a month after squeezing into the FTSE 100, electronic rentals group Thorn is in danger of losing its place among the UK's top stocks at Wednesday's quarterly shake-up of constituents, analysts said on Tuesday .
Almost certain to replace it will be newly merged auto components group LucasVarity Plc after trading began in its shares last Friday.
But this month's review looks likely to be a low key affair, with only Courtaulds Plc and Southern Electric Plc also under threat of losing their FTSE 100 status.
Thorn narrowly pushed industrial conglomerate Cookson Plc out of the blue-chip index just over three weeks ago after the break-up of music and retail group Thorn EMI.
Since then the shares have struggled, slipping back from a best of 409p, to Monday's close of 383p.
That drop in the share price will probably be enough to see the shares slip out of the list of Britain's largest companies.

A company qualifies for automatic inclusion in the FTSE 100 if, as LucasVarity does, it ranks among the top 90 in terms of market capitalisation. It then replaces the lowest ranking index constituent.
Alternatively, if companies currently in the index fall below 110 in the list they will be replaced by the next largest company.

At Monday's close, Thorn ranked 114, Southern Electric 111 and Courtaulds 109. FTSE International, the body which oversees Britain's market indices meets on Wednesday to discuss the changes which will be based on Tuesday's closing prices.
British Land Co and REXAM are among the leading candidates to take a place in the FTSE 100 should either Courtaulds or Southern Electric fall out.
A number of changes to the second line index, the FTSE mid-250 are also expected.
Shares in nuclear generator British Energy are set to make it into the index after its listing on the London stock market back in July.
Other newcomers expected to break into the mid-250 include Sun Life & Provincial Holdings, Somerfield and Pace Micro Technology.
Taking the step up from the SmallCap index to the mid-250 are likely to be Cairn Energy, Greene King, Johnston Press, and Inspec.
Among the stocks which could make way for them are troubled food retailer Iceland Group, Marston Thompson & Evershed and Berisford.
